bullets.title: Warsh Jackson Hole speech: market pricing 54% risk-on, Warsh likely to avoid fresh policy signals
bullets.body: Macro investors see Warsh's willingness to use the Fed funds rate to tighten financial conditions as the key question: 37.5% expect hawkish tone, 37.5% neutral, 25% dovish. A dominant 65% view is Warsh delivers a process/institutional reform speech without fresh signals — read as a dovish dodge that would support Gold/Bitcoin/risk-off factors and weaken USD. If Warsh anchors 10yr yields, EPS momentum and GARP factors benefit; if he defers to markets, easy financial conditions and lower real yields follow. Fed officials remain divided: Collins open to a rate hike if disinflation stalls; Schmid says rates aren't restraining the economy; JPM tactically bullish but with lower conviction ahead of speech at 10am ET.

bullets.title: NVDA posts record Q2 $96B revenue (+106% YoY), guides Q3 $108B; single-day market cap gain of ~$500B
bullets.body: NVDA's blowout Q2 print — record $96B revenue (+106% YoY), net income $59.7B (+126%), 66% net margin — drove its second-largest single-day US equity gain ever, adding ~$500B in market cap and contributing +33% of SPY's +0.7% return. Q3 guidance of ~$108B implies ~89% YoY growth. Trump publicly congratulated Jensen Huang. NVDA paused its revenue-sharing cloud financing program (announced July) over antitrust concerns; company denies a permanent pause. NVDA also agreed to acquire Hugging Face for $12.9B and launched a PAC.

bullets.title: Semiconductor premarket weakness: MRVL -8%, SNDK breaks trend; broader semi names down 1-3%
bullets.body: MRVL's Q2 beat/raise (revenue $2.74B +37% YoY, FY27 raised to $12B, FY28 to $18B with 50% YoY growth) is being sold as the print came in below elevated expectations — Google warrant deal upside is back-end loaded to FY29+, gross margin guided 57.5-58.5% in Q3 (slight miss), and FCF fell short. Sell-side remains 86% Buy with avg PT $286.85. SNDK broke its Hedgeye TREND; MU, STX, INTC, COHR, CRDO, NBIS, AXTI, LITE, WDC down 1-3% in premarket. Equal-weight S&P ended down ~100bp vs benchmark despite headline index gains — semis/software breadth poor with NVDA driving essentially all index alpha.

bullets.title: Software renaissance: IGV +47% from April lows, expensive software factor +7.6% day; SaaS fears ease
bullets.body: CRM surged 22.5%, CRWD +20.5%, OKTA +28%, PANW +12.8% in recent sessions as AI monetization evidence (CRM first cRPO beat in 3 quarters, Workday AI ARR $600M +200% YoY, RBRK NNARR +35% YoY) outweighs AI disruption fears. UBS/Piper note absence of meaningful competitive threats from frontier AI vendors is improving SaaS sentiment; software L/S ratio at 4th percentile since 2018 provides room to run. iShares Software ETF hit YTD highs and is up 47% from April lows.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler AI capex: $1.2T+ 2027 off-balance-sheet spend; crowding out risk building
bullets.body: MS notes hyperscalers are spending $1.2T+ capex in 2027 via off-balance-sheet financing, raising FCF overstatement risk. Hedgeye flags NVDA has disclosed $105B additional financial guarantees backing OpenAI lease obligations, with $800B total AI supply chain guarantees per BIS. Treasury + IG issuance (hyperscaler debt) net of QE/buybacks is approaching record levels, approaching crowding-out conditions that exceed 2020-21 crisis peaks. Concerns raised that CoreWeave/neoclouds requiring repeated debt issuance could trigger AI selloff if refinancing difficulties emerge.

bullets.title: Memory shortage extended to 2030: SK Hynix CEO dismisses oversupply risk; SNDK/Kioxia commit $31B
bullets.body: SK Hynix CEO stated memory chip shortage will persist through end of 2030, describing AI-era memory as no longer a commodity. SNDK and Kioxia plan $31B+ investment in Japan manufacturing through 2032. Samsung leads Nvidia's NVHBM supply following HBM4 development, and SK Hynix is breaking ground on a $4B+ Indiana HBM packaging plant (targeting H2 2029 mass production) with $458M in federal CHIPS Act funding.

bullets.title: AI capex risk: Wolfe warns voter backlash won't derail near-term data center buildout, but 2028 cycle is risk
bullets.body: Voter support for local data center construction fell 60 points over 12 months, with opposition now exceeding coal and nuclear. State-level moratoria (NY, TX, PA) won't stop construction as exemptions protect in-progress projects. Federal restrictions unlikely during Trump's term; however, 2028 presents greater uncertainty as both parties may field candidates with mixed AI views. Data center developers can afford to offer incentives to localities. Grid connection wait times in the US average 3.7 years, representing an infrastructure bottleneck ahead of any physical deployment.

bullets.title: European inflation picking up on energy: France HICP 2.7%, Spain 4.5% in August; ECB September hike nearly certain
bullets.body: French HICP accelerated 0.3pt to 2.7% YoY in August; Spanish HICP surged 0.6pt to 4.5% YoY. Energy inflation drove the spike — France at 16.7% YoY, Spain ~17% YoY — tied to re-intensification of Middle East conflict. Core inflation edged lower in both countries. JPMorgan projects euro area flash HICP rising 0.4pt to 3.3% in August. Another ECB rate hike in September is described as 'almost a done deal.' German 10-year Bund yield hit highest level in 15+ years.

bullets.title: US wages fall to 43% of gross domestic income — lowest since Great Depression; corporate profits at record
bullets.body: Wages and salaries dropped to ~43% of US gross domestic income in Q1 2026, the lowest level since the start of the Great Depression. Morgan Stanley notes Q2 nonfinancial corporate profits surged $400.9B as firms raised per-unit prices substantially while holding labor and nonlabor costs flat — margin expansion mirroring COVID-era dynamics. MS expects normalization as inflation recedes and labor costs firm.

bullets.title: Strait of Hormuz partially reopened: flows recover to 7-8 mbpd vs. 4 mbpd in July; Brent settles $89.70
bullets.body: Kuwait and Qatar restored crude shipments to ~70% of pre-war levels using shuttle operations through the Strait of Hormuz; total flows recovered from ~4 mbpd in mid-July to 7-8 mbpd. CENTCOM confirmed international shipping lanes are open and mines have been cleared, but vessel traffic on Thursday stood at only 5 vs. the 10-day avg of 15. Brent settled +2.1% at $89.70/bbl; White House rejected return to June MOU terms with Iran. US natural gas futures +2.3% to $2.907/MMBtu.

bullets.title: Chip tariff risk emerging: Trump admin weighing sweeping tariffs on semis, laptops, gaming consoles, DC servers
bullets.body: Jefferies and Roth note the Trump administration is weighing broader semiconductor tariffs including laptops, gaming consoles, and data center servers. This risk is cited as a key overhang for the semi supply chain alongside the NVDA-led 'despeccing' efforts, even as NVDA's blowout quarter reinforces near-term AI demand.

bullets.title: Hedgeye US inflation nowcast at 3.50% YoY; CPI release Sept 11; Middle East energy driving volatility
bullets.body: Hedgeye's August CPI nowcast came in at +3.50% YoY, +14bps sequentially from the prior month, citing Middle East energy market disruption as the primary driver of inflation volatility. The model has 90% directional accuracy on CPI acceleration/deceleration. CPI release is scheduled for September 11.

bullets.title: US midterm risk: split Congress consensus may shift policy focus to Executive Action and fiscal battles
bullets.body: Jefferies notes the consensus view is for a split Congress post-November midterms, which would limit major legislation and shift activity to executive action, congressional oversight, fiscal battles, and state-level developments. Investors may be underestimating policy implications for 2027-2028. Europe faces additional risk: AfD polling at 40% in Saxony-Anhalt ahead of September 6 vote; four of EU's five largest members hold elections in 2027, creating EU budget and Russia/Ukraine policy uncertainty.

bullets.title: Euro area economic sentiment rose to 98.4 in August; manufacturing, services, consumer all improved
bullets.body: European Commission economic sentiment index rose 1.3pts to 98.4 in August, signaling above-potential growth at ~1.4% annualized, consistent with recent GDP reports. Employment intentions improved. Pricing intentions moderated, consistent with 2.5% underlying price pressure. France's Q2 GDP was flat QoQ (0.0% vs 0.2% est) dragged by inventory; Sweden Q2 GDP surprised at +3.3% YoY vs 2.5% est. Switzerland KOF leading indicator beat strongly at 106.7 vs 103.0 est.

bullets.title: Jackson Hole: tail risk cheaply priced; CTAs stretched short in Treasuries; options market underpricing surprise
bullets.body: One macro strategist notes the options market is underpricing tail risk ahead of Warsh's speech, with CTAs stretched short in Treasuries and potentially vulnerable to a surprise hawkish move. Gold fell ahead of the speech as investors took profits; JPM recommends tactically trimming gold into the event given narrative intensity at recent highs. 7-year Treasury auction cleared near 2-year highs.

bullets.title: AFRM +13% post-earnings: GMV +36% YoY, consumer spending healthy, positive read for V/MA and payment peers
bullets.body: Affirm reported Q4 revenue $1.17B (beat $1.11B est), GMV +36% YoY to $14.1B, with Affirm Card GMV +124% YoY to $2.8B representing 20% of total GMV. Active merchants +51%, active consumers +21%. FY27 GMV guidance >$64B (+27%). RLTC 8% above Street; operating income 9% ahead. Citi and Jefferies see positive read-through to V/MA on sustained consumer strength; AFRM only 32% penetrated among top e-commerce firms.

bullets.title: Meta settles 48-state child safety lawsuit for $18B over 10 years; product changes create engagement risk
bullets.body: Meta settled a federal lawsuit with 48 US states for ~$18B over 10 years covering addictive design and child data collection practices — a fraction of the potential $1.4T penalty. Settlement removes risk of adverse bellwether verdict but does not affect thousands of other federal, state, and local cases. Meta agreed to stronger parental controls, usage limits, and content restrictions that could affect engagement and monetization.

bullets.title: Data center supply constraint: AI infrastructure cycle constrained by grid access and delivery, not demand
bullets.body: Grid connection wait times in the US average 3.7 years ahead of physical deployment. IREN's FY26 call highlighted AI infrastructure constrained by physical delivery, grid access, and capital formation — not customer demand — validating supply-side investment theses. Liquid cooling and 800V DC are becoming baseline specs; legacy air-cooled capacity faces accelerating obsolescence, benefiting Vertiv.

bullets.title: Anthropic IPO targeted for late Sept/early Oct; investor day mid-September; prospectus after Labor Day
bullets.body: Anthropic is expected to host an investor day in mid-September ahead of a likely late-September or early-October IPO. The company is mulling allowing shareholders to sell in the offering and plans an extended lockup to manage post-listing volatility. Separately, a US judge ruled the Pentagon's ban on Anthropic AI for federal agencies was unlawful.

bullets.title: S&P 500 entering seasonally worst month of year; advance-decline line near May lows despite headline gains
bullets.body: S&P settled at 7,731 (+0.72%) while NASDAQ rose +1.56%; however, the equal-weight S&P ended down ~100bps vs the benchmark on the day, with the index driven almost entirely by NVDA. The 10-day advance-decline line is near its lowest since May. Seasonally, the coming month is the only calendar month averaging negative total returns for the S&P 500 since 2010. SPX immediate risk range 7,620-7,788; UST 10yr yield 4.60-4.76%.
